title: Talking About Your Design
vocab: We changed the shape to improve the user experience.
We found this issue during prototype testing.
look at two or more things to find differences
We compared our design with three competitors.
We changed the structure to reduce the weight.
find a good middle point between different needs
We need to balance design, cost, and performance.
phrases: Based on our research, users want a lighter laptop.
The main reason is to improve the user experience.
I worked closely with the mechanical engineering team.
question: Why did you choose this design?
model: The main goal was to make the laptop look thinner and cleaner. Based on our research, users wanted a simple design that was easy to carry. We compared several competitor products. So I decided to simplify the rear design. This helped us create a cleaner and more modern product.
shadow: We need to balance design, cost, and performance.

title: Working With Engineering
vocab: We needed more space for the cooling system.
We made a small change to the rear cover.
The new frame is stronger than the old one.
a way to solve a problem
We found a simple solution with the ME team.
phrases: I understand the issue. Let’s check the possible options.
We tested several options before making the final decision.
This was the best balance between design and engineering.
question: How do you work with engineers when they ask you to change your design?
model: First, I try to understand the engineering issue. Then I work with the ME team to explore several options. We compare the impact on design, cost, and performance. Finally, we choose the option with the best balance. I try to keep the original design intent as much as possible.
shadow: We tested several options before making the final decision.

title: Production Handoff
vocab: a product used for checking quality
We checked the first production sample.
a small space between two parts
The gap was larger than the golden sample.
Cosmetic quality is important for a premium product.
look carefully to make sure something is correct
We checked the color and surface finish.
I approved the sample after the final review.
phrases: Compared with the golden sample, the gap is too visible.
I would like to check more production samples.
Before mass production, we need to confirm the cosmetic quality.
question: What do you check before approving a production sample?
model: First, I compare the sample with the approved golden sample. I check the color, texture, gap, flush, and surface quality. If I find an issue, I work with the supplier and engineering team to find the cause. I also check more samples to make sure the quality is stable. I approve the product only when the result meets our design target.
shadow: Before mass production, we need to confirm the cosmetic quality.

title: Competitor Analysis
vocab: compare products to learn what works well
This feature makes the product easier to use.
a small part of a design
We studied the hinge detail carefully.
Our solution should feel different from the competitor.
The study gave us a useful design insight.
phrases: What we learned was that users notice the rear profile first.
Instead of copying the form, we used the same design principle.
Our opportunity is to make the product feel lighter and cleaner.
question: What did you learn from competitor products?
model: We compared several competitor laptops. We noticed that many of them used large rear vents for cooling. The main insight was that thermal performance often makes the product look heavier. Instead of copying their form, we looked for a cleaner solution. Our opportunity was to keep strong cooling performance with a lighter visual feel.
shadow: Instead of copying the form, we used the same design principle.

title: Material Selection
vocab: what a product is made from

The new material reduced the weight.
the money needed to make something
We needed to control the manufacturing cost.
the final surface look and feel
The matte finish feels more premium.
able to last a long time
The material needs to be durable for daily use.
phrases: From a design point of view…
From a design point of view, aluminum gives a more premium feel.
The trade-off is higher cost and lower weight.

question: Why did you choose aluminum instead of plastic?
model: The main reason was product positioning. Aluminum gives the product a more premium feel and better stiffness. The trade-off is higher cost. We also considered weight, surface quality, and durability. In the end, we chose aluminum because it supported the user experience and brand image.
shadow: I would evaluate cost, weight, strength, and user perception.

model: First, I ask why the change is needed. I want to understand the exact clearance or structure issue. Then we explore several options together. title: Design Review
vocab: I explained the design decision to the team.
why something happens or is chosen
The main reason was better usability.

phrases: Let me explain the reason behind this design direction.
My main concern is the visual thickness.

question: How do you defend a design decision in a review?
model: I start with the user need and product goal. Then I show research, competitor examples, and prototype results. I explain the reason behind the design decision in simple terms. I also listen to engineering and PM feedback. Finally, I recommend the option that gives the best overall balance.
shadow: I recommend this option because it gives the best overall balance.

title: Cost Reduction
vocab: use less money, time, or material
This change can save manufacturing cost.

We checked the impact on user experience.
how useful or important something is
This detail adds visual value to the product.
phrases: 我們能否在不影響…的情況下降低成本
Can we reduce cost without hurting the user experience?
This detail adds value because users touch it every day.
I would not change it unless…
I would not change it unless we can keep the same quality.
question: How do you respond to a cost reduction request?
model: First, I understand the cost target. Then I identify which parts have the biggest cost impact. I protect the user-facing details that are important to quality and brand value. I explore simpler geometry, materials, or processes. I recommend the option that saves cost with the least impact on user experience.
shadow: Can we reduce cost without hurting the user experience?

title: User-Centered Design
theme_zh: 以使用者為中心的設計
vocab: the person who uses the product
We talked with users before starting the design.
The main user need was better portability.
We improved the grip for better comfort.
The control should be easy to understand.
how a person feels when using a product
We wanted to improve the overall user experience.
phrases: Users told us the product felt too heavy.
The key user need was easy portability.
This helps users carry the product more comfortably.
question: How do you use user research in your design process?
model: We talked with users and studied how they used the product. We learned that weight and portability were important. The key need was easier daily carry. So I reduced unnecessary volume and improved the grip area. This helped users feel more comfortable and confident with the product.
shadow: The key user need was easy portability.

question: Can you walk me through one of your projects?
model: The goal of this project was to create a thinner and cleaner gaming laptop. The biggest challenge was limited space for cooling. My role was to lead the industrial design and keep the visual direction consistent. I worked closely with ME, thermal, PM, and suppliers. In the end, we delivered a design that balanced performance, cost, and user experience.
